title: Harden org/team onboarding controls: domain assertions + email blocking
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: New orgs and teams are able to onboard with weak email/domain checks leading to mistaken tenant joins and manual remediation. We need stronger, low-friction controls that combine domain verification assertions, configurable allow/deny email lists, and adaptive invite throttling tied into RBAC v2 and SSO enrollment flows. This ticket scopes implementation of the invite policy enforcement surface, audit logging hooks, and migration steps for existing org settings.
proposed_solution: 1) Add 'domain_assertion' state to org metadata that reflects verified methods (DNS/TXT, MX, SAML issuer). 2) Introduce a first-class allowlist/denylist resource scoped to orgs and teams with pattern matching (suffix, regex). 3) Enforce allow/deny checks at invite issuance and at SSO/auto-join events with an extensible policy engine. 4) Emit structured audit events for every invite decision (allowed/blocked/auto-revoked) to the central audit service. 5) Tie behavior to RBAC v2: org admins with 'invite:override' permission can bypass but overrides are logged and require justification. 6) Provide console UX to surface domain health, sample verification steps, and an audit view for recent invite actions.
design_decisions: - Use existing audit log schema but add 'invite_decision' event type and fields: actor, target_email, rule_id, rule_type, rationale, outcome. - Prefer server-side enforcement over client-side UI blocks to prevent race conditions with SSO providers. - Allowlist precedence: explicit denylist > allowlist > domain assertion. - For SAML/SSO: if SSO enforces attribute-based emails, treat SAML issuer-domain pairing as a lightweight assertion and require DNS verification for full domain claim. - Keep migration read-only for 2 weeks and notify admins via in-app banner before automatic enforcement.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): deploy policy engine + audit events to 5% of orgs; monitor invite block rate and false positives for 72 hours. Stage 2: enable allowlist/denylist UI as 'suggested' (not enforced) for 24 hours. Stage 3: flip enforcement for orgs with admin opt-in or those meeting criteria (>=10 seats, enterprise plan). Stage 4: global enforcement and deprecation of legacy invite heuristics. Feature flag: org_onboard_policy_v2.
acceptance_criteria: Server rejects invite when email matches denylist pattern and generates invite_decision audit event
Server accepts invite if email matches allowlist or verified domain assertion and logs decision
RBAC override path requires justification and produces audit event with justification field
Console shows domain assertion status and last 30 invite_decision events for the org
No regression in SSO-based auto-join flows (less than 0.5% increase in failures during canary)
Load test demonstrating negligible latency impact (<5ms median) on invite flow under typical QPS
migration_steps: Backfill domain_assertion from existing domain_verifications table into new org metadata (read-only phase)
Import existing allow/deny patterns from admin_settings into new allowlist/denylist resource with admin notification
Run a 14-day monitoring job to surface candidate false-positives and email org admins with opt-in instructions
Switch enforcement flag after manual review windows expire
observability: Dashboards: Invite decisions by outcome, top blocked domains, per-org block rate. Alerts: spike in blocked_invites > 50% of baseline or SSO auto-join failures increased by >1%. Trace additions: tag invite request traces with rule_id and decision for waterfall analysis.
security_review_notes: Security will validate audit retention and ensure fields do not leak PII in logs. We will redact local-part of emails in telemetry unless org has explicit data-retention-waiver. KMS-backed signing for domain assertion records to prevent tampering.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives block legitimate users. Mitigation: staged rollout, 'suggested' mode, admin override with automatic alert to security. Risk: audit log storage growth. Mitigation: aggregate daily summaries + retention policy for raw events (90 days).
